steps: Mendeleev arranged elements in order of increasing atomic masses, whereas the modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic numbers.

Mendeleev’s periodic law stated that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses. The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
Mendeleev’s table had 8 groups, each divided into subgroups A and B. The modern periodic table has 18 groups.
Mendeleev’s table left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties. The modern table includes the elements discovered later in their appropriate positions.

The positions of isotopes could not be explained in Mendeleev’s table because isotopes have different atomic masses. In the modern periodic table, isotopes occupy the same position because they have the same atomic number.
Some elements did not fit the order of increasing atomic masses in Mendeleev’s table. Their positions are explained in the modern table by arranging elements according to atomic number.
items.finalAnswer: The modern periodic table improves upon Mendeleev’s table by arranging elements according to atomic number, which explains their proper positions and periodic properties.
